Type locality. “ The banks of the Strickland River, about 100 miles above the junction with the Fly River ”, Western Province, Papua New Guinea (Troughton, 1937 a: 124). It seems conceivable that Troughton obtained locality data of the holotype from his contemporary Froggatt. Dwyer et al. (2015) concluded that “ Fossil camp ” was the furthest upstream location on the Strickland River reached by the Geographical Society’s Expedition, located between the junctions of the Murray and Carrington Rivers at approximately 5 ° 51 ' 20 " S 142 ° 8 ' 50 " E, and they state that Froggatt had estimated this site to be about 100 miles (along the river) from the junction with the Fly River. The Expedition stayed one night at Fossil Camp (27 September 1885) and returned to the Fly junction on 29 September. It is likely that the holotype was collected in late September, and the type locality was Fossil Camp or an adjoining site downstream.
